summary: This is a reference page for the DROP USER command, which removes a specified user from the system. It gives the syntax with an optional IF EXISTS clause and explains that the name identifier must be double-quoted if it contains spaces, special or mixed-case characters, which makes it case-sensitive. The usage notes state that dropped users cannot be recovered and that worksheets and dashboards owned by the dropped user are also removed, with an alternative of setting DISABLED = TRUE mentioned. The only example is DROP USER user1;.
one_line: Reference page for the DROP USER command, which permanently removes a user and their owned worksheets and dashboards.
key_facts: The DROP USER command removes the specified user from the system.
The syntax is DROP USER [ IF EXISTS ] <name>.
The <name> parameter specifies the identifier for the user to drop.
If the identifier contains spaces, special characters, or mixed-case characters, the entire string must be enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
Dropped users cannot be recovered; they must be recreated.
When a user is dropped, the worksheets and dashboards owned by that user are also removed.
The usage notes suggest an alternative to dropping a user, using DISABLED = TRUE instead.
The page gives two options for retaining access to worksheets owned by a user, though the option details are not included in the note.
The example in the note is DROP USER user1;.
The page is listed under User Management, Database Role Management, Account-level Role Management, and Privilege Management in its navigation breadcrumb.
